Atlas of Civilization · experimental world 01

Angkor Mandala Lab

A runnable, uncalibrated mechanism laboratory for agricultural intensification, hydraulic vulnerability and overlapping spheres of political allegiance. One simulation covers 750–1500 CE without scheduling a rise or collapse.

Scientific status: The geography, coefficients, populations and institutions are synthetic. Results are outcomes of assumptions, not predictions of Khmer history. The reference run currently overshoots the archaeological population estimate and fails to generate Angkor as the dominant polity throughout its historical peak. Those failures are useful diagnostics.

Which court draws each community?

What each experiment changes

The hydraulic dependency hypothesis is currently hard-coded as a strut. Next test: substitute household ponds and drainage for central reservoir investment, then compare likelihood of enduring urban concentration under randomized climate.

Research anchors

Klassen et al. (2021), diachronic population modeling · Klassen et al. (2022), agro-urban spatial equilibrium · Lucero et al. / Angkor hydraulic research, cascading network failure · Bennett (2022), spatial historical state model.

Files: angkor.py, tests, scenario JSON and a reproducible build script. Simulation uses a seeded numerical RNG. To change coefficients and run new experiments, run the Python package locally. Generated toy values are not archaeological estimates. v0.1.
